title: Release needlepoint: Microrelease ceremony & signal synthesis (lab notebook)
body:
Purpose and quick context:

This is a lightweight working notebook for a very narrow (needlepoint) microrelease ceremony pattern that we've been iterating on. Aim: ship sub-1% traffic microreleases for LLM features with short feedback loops but high signal fidelity across cross-functional stakeholders. This doc captures the ritual, signal stitching, and a practical checklist — intentionally informal.

Key goals (short):
- Get a fast yes/no within 48 hours for low-risk changes (prompt tweaks, reranker weights, heuristic filters).
- Maintain cost latency safety: ensure per-token cost delta < 10% and P99 latency within SLO.
- Catch quality regressions (hallucination/fluency/toxicity) on a curated eval prompt set.

Ceremony roles (minimal):
- Release steward (owner): rotates weekly — owns rollout orchestration, slack pings, rollback. (example: Asha)
- Signal owner(s): product owner + ML engineer owning eval sets.
- Oncall SRE: watches infra metrics and executes capacity rollback.
- Observability buddy: pairs with steward for dashboarding + commit of notes.

Preflight (day 0):
- Smoke: run full synthetic smoke (core flows) on staging with traffic-replay.
- Eval baseline: run canonical eval prompts (200 prompts across domains) and record baseline metrics: semantic precision, hallucination rate, toxicity flagged, reranker precision@10, average tokens/generated, kv-cache hit rate.
- Cost/latency check: simulated 1000 qps with model variant; capture median and P95/P99 latency and estimated token cost per 1M tokens.

Microrelease plan (stepwise):
1) Canary slice (0.1%): 30 min baseline observation. Check health: error rate, latency P99, token cost.
2) Signal sweep (0.1% -> 1% over 4 hours): increment exposures every 30–60 min, gather both telemetry and eval sample snapshots.
3) Confirm or abort: after reaching 1% or earlier if safety triggers fire.

Signal stitching: what we measure and why:
- Infra: errors/second, 95/99 latency, cpu/gpu utilization, autoscaler events.
- Cost: projected token cost delta (per 100k requests), cache hit delta.
- Quality (weighted):
  - Semantic regression score: pairwise utility tests + human QA on 50 hits.
  - Hallucination rate: prompts with factual ground truth (automated check + spot human review).
  - Safety flags: toxicity model triggers per 1k responses.
  - Behavioral drift: changed response length distribution, abnormal repeated tokens.
- Business signals: feature-specific KPIs (CTR, completion-to-action), if available for the sample slice.

Decision heuristics (quick rules we use when time is short):
- Abort immediately if: 5xx error rate > 0.5% above baseline OR latency P99 > SLO + 200ms OR token cost > baseline + 20% for sustained 30m window.
- Hold and investigate if: semantic regression > 4% (on the weighted eval) OR toxicity flags double baseline.
- Proceed if: no hard aborts, quality metrics within 2% of baseline, and human spot-check (5 examples) looks fine.

A/B considerations for LLM features (practical tips):
- Use interleaved sampling for reranks / ranking changes to avoid slice contamination.
- For generative A/Bs, measure both automated metrics and a small human-in-the-loop panel; trust automated signals for infra but rely on human panel to catch subtle behavior drift.
- Ensure randomization key is stable across sessions to avoid sampling bias.

Observability checklist (dashboards + alerts):
- Canary dashboard shows: traffic slice id, errors, latency percentiles, tokens per request, kv-cache hit, model variant.
- Quality scoreboard (rolling 6h): semantic regression, hallucination rate, toxicity rate, human-flagged fails.
- Alerts to page: infra hard aborts; automatic cost guard triggers (threshold-based and rate-of-change based).

Runbook snippets (copyable):
- Quick rollback: endpoint switch to stable variant -> scale down, confirm 0 errors -> notify.
- Emergency: run re-route to lower-tier model (saves cost and latency) if GPU OOM or disk pressure observed.

Open questions / things to iterate on:
- How big should the human QA panel be to get reliable signal for semantic regression on 1% exposure? Current guess: 50–100 examples curated from failing buckets.
- Should we incorporate active sampling (adversarial prompts) during early exposure to stress the model? Pros: catches failure modes. Cons: noisy for business metrics.
- Is the cost delta heuristic (10% threshold) too conservative for high-value features? Consider tiered thresholds by feature value.

Immediate action items (owner in parens):
- Bake a tiny dashboard template (observability buddy: Marcus)
- Add a preflight script to replay 1k canonical prompts during staging (eng-runtime: Evelyn)
- Draft a short oncall cheat-sheet for rollback steps (SRE: Diego)

Notes to self / stray thoughts:
- Keep ceremony light: ideal path is steward + 1 engineer + SRE on shift. Too many cooks slow the loop.
- We should tag all microrelease slices with metadata (feature, steward, eval-run-id) to make postmortems easier.
- Consider a "soft-fallback" route where low-severity regressions trigger automatic temporary token-limiting rather than full abort, to avoid noisy rollbacks.

Appendix: quick template for microrelease announcement (Slack)
- header: "Microrelease: <feature> — steward @<name> — target: 1% over 4h"
- bullets: preflight pass status, linked dashboards, critical abort rules, minimal human check (y/n)

End of notebook. This remains intentionally terse. Drop notes, test results, and links below as we run experiments.
